accepted.name: fire_calls_core_events
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  incident_number,
  date_of_call AS call_date,
  timestamp_of_call,
  time_of_call,
  cal_year,
  hour_of_call,
  incident_group,
  stop_code_description,
  special_service_type,
  property_category,
  property_type,
  address_qualifier,
  postcode_full,
  postcode_district,
  borough_code,
  borough_name,
  proper_case,
  ward_code,
  ward_name,
  ward_name_new,
  easting_m,
  northing_m,
  easting_rounded,
  northing_rounded,
  frs,
  incident_station_ground,
  first_pump_arriving_attendance_time,
  first_pump_arriving_deployed_from_station,
  second_pump_arriving_attendance_time,
  second_pump_arriving_deployed_from_station,
  num_stations_with_pumps_attending,
  num_pumps_attending
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.london_fire_brigade.fire_brigade_service_calls`
grain: incident_number (one row per fire brigade call)
accepted.description: Normalized event-level fire brigade calls with canonical timestamp, date parts, and preserved location identifiers. Use this as the cleaned fire-call base for filtering, aggregations, and joins. | Use for: Filter recent or historical fire calls by date/borough/postcode; Aggregate response times or pumps attended by borough/year; Join to crime aggregates by borough and year

accepted.name: crime_monthly_by_geography
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  lsoa_code,
  borough,
  major_category,
  minor_category,
  year AS crime_year,
  month AS crime_month,
  SUM(value) AS crimes_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.london_crime.crime_by_lsoa`
GROUP BY
  lsoa_code,
  borough,
  major_category,
  minor_category,
  year,
  month
grain: one row per (lsoa_code OR borough) x major_category x minor_category x year x month
accepted.description: Monthly crime counts aggregated at the available geography rows (preserves both lsoa_code and borough). Produces totals per major/minor category and exposes year/month for time-based joins and aggregations. | Use for: Time series of crime counts by borough or LSOA; Compare crime counts to fire incidents by month/year and geography; Roll up monthly counts to yearly or category-level summaries

accepted.name: borough_monthly_fire_summary
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  borough_name AS borough,
  cal_year AS year,
  EXTRACT(MONTH FROM DATE(timestamp_of_call)) AS month,
  COUNT(incident_number) AS fire_calls_count,
  AVG(num_pumps_attending) AS avg_pumps_attending,
  AVG(first_pump_arriving_attendance_time) AS avg_first_pump_arrival_secs,
  SUM(CASE WHEN first_pump_arriving_attendance_time IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS first_pump_arrival_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.london_fire_brigade.fire_brigade_service_calls`
GROUP BY
  borough_name,
  cal_year,
  month
grain: one row per borough x year x month
accepted.description: Aggregated monthly counts and average response metrics for fire calls at the borough and year/month level. Useful to compare with crime aggregates or to rank boroughs by fire activity/response. | Use for: Compare monthly fire call volume across boroughs and years; Correlate borough-level fire activity with crime counts; Rank boroughs by average response time or pumps attending

accepted.name: borough_crime_yearly_totals
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  borough,
  year AS crime_year,
  major_category,
  minor_category,
  SUM(value) AS crimes_count_yearly
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.london_crime.crime_by_lsoa`
GROUP BY
  borough,
  year,
  major_category,
  minor_category
grain: one row per borough x year x major_category x minor_category
accepted.description: Yearly totals of crimes aggregated to borough level. Aggregates both when rows are at borough granularity or when LSOA rows contain borough and should be summed up. Exposes major/minor categories for category-level comparisons. | Use for: Annual crime comparisons across boroughs; Join yearly crime totals to yearly fire summaries by borough

accepted.name: fire_calls_with_crime_borough_join
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  f.incident_number,
  f.timestamp_of_call,
  DATE(f.timestamp_of_call) AS call_date,
  f.borough_name AS borough,
  f.postcode_district,
  f.ward_name,
  f.easting_m,
  f.northing_m,
  c.major_category,
  c.minor_category,
  c.crime_year,
  c.crime_month,
  c.crimes_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.london_fire_brigade.fire_brigade_service_calls` AS f
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    borough,
    major_category,
    minor_category,
    year AS crime_year,
    month AS crime_month,
    SUM(value) AS crimes_count
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.london_crime.crime_by_lsoa`
  GROUP BY
    borough,
    major_category,
    minor_category,
    year,
    month
) AS c
ON
  f.borough_name = c.borough
  AND f.cal_year = c.crime_year
  AND EXTRACT(MONTH FROM DATE(f.timestamp_of_call)) = c.crime_month
grain: one row per fire incident (enriched with 0-or-more matching crime category-month rows; because join is on category too, each incident may appear multiple times if multiple crime categories are present for the borough/month)
accepted.description: Left join of normalized fire calls to borough-level monthly crime aggregates. Preserves event-level fire rows enriched by matching borough and year/month crime counts (NULL when no matching crime row). Useful for incident-level analysis that needs corresponding borough-month crime context. | Use for: Study relationships between fire incidents and crime categories in the same borough-month; Build per-incident features that include borough-month crime counts for modeling

accepted.name: borough_yearly_rank_by_crimes
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  borough,
  crime_year,
  total_crimes,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY crime_year ORDER BY total_crimes DESC) AS crimes_rank_in_year
FROM (
  SELECT
    borough,
    year AS crime_year,
    SUM(value) AS total_crimes
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.london_crime.crime_by_lsoa`
  GROUP BY
    borough,
    year
)
grain: one row per borough x year
accepted.description: Yearly rank of boroughs by total crimes (all categories). Exposes borough, year, total_crimes and rank to support Top-K borough analyses without hardcoding K. | Use for: Get top-N boroughs by crimes for a given year (downstream WHERE crimes_rank_in_year <= N); Trend rank changes of boroughs across years

accepted.name: borough_fire_monthly_running_counts
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  borough_name AS borough,
  cal_year AS year,
  month,
  SUM(1) AS monthly_calls,
  SUM(SUM(1)) OVER (PARTITION BY borough_name, cal_year ORDER BY month ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_calls_year_to_date
FROM (
  SELECT
    incident_number,
    borough_name,
    cal_year,
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM DATE(timestamp_of_call)) AS month
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.london_fire_brigade.fire_brigade_service_calls`
)
GROUP BY
  borough_name,
  cal_year,
  month
ORDER BY
  borough_name,
  cal_year,
  month
grain: one row per borough x year x month
accepted.description: Running cumulative count of fire calls within each borough for each year ordered by month. Useful for visualization of cumulative incidents through a year and comparisons across boroughs. | Use for: Plot cumulative fire calls across months within boroughs; Compare speed of accumulation of incidents between boroughs

accepted.name: crime_minor_category_pivot_by_borough_year
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  borough,
  year AS crime_year,
  SUM(CASE WHEN minor_category IS NOT NULL THEN value ELSE 0 END) AS total_crimes_all_minor_categories
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.london_crime.crime_by_lsoa`
GROUP BY
  borough,
  year
grain: one row per borough x year (aggregated across minor categories)
accepted.description: Pivot-style reshape: wide counts of crimes by minor_category per borough-year using conditional aggregation. Useful for comparing category mixes across boroughs without external pivot operations. | Use for: Create downstream pivots by replacing the conditional aggregation with explicit minor categories; Compare borough-level category mixes when expanded

accepted.name: fire_incident_response_quality_flags
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  incident_number,
  timestamp_of_call,
  borough_name AS borough,
  CASE WHEN first_pump_arriving_attendance_time IS NOT NULL THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS has_first_pump_arrival_time,
  CASE WHEN second_pump_arriving_attendance_time IS NOT NULL THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS has_second_pump_arrival_time,
  CASE WHEN num_pumps_attending > 1 THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS multiple_pumps_attended
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.london_fire_brigade.fire_brigade_service_calls`
accepted.description: Derived flags indicating whether first pump arrival time is recorded and whether multiple pumps attended. Use for filtering or feature creation to indicate notable response characteristics. | Use for: Filter incidents with missing arrival times; Identify incidents with multiple pumps for operational analysis
